headline: A comedian sent his own AI stand-in to a job interview run by an AI recruiter, and the two bots ended up arguing over his pay and trapped in a goodbye loop.
score_reason: Light, widely shareable story with a real point about AI agents negotiating for people; single outlet, staged video.
importance_line: It shows, in a staged video, that an AI sent to speak for a person can misstate their record and undersell their pay, which matters to job seekers and to firms now selling AI negotiating agents; it is one comedian's video, not a study.
summary: The Register reports that comedian Graham Dot Zip, who is known on YouTube for trolling AI job-interview bots, sent his own AI representative, Victor, to be interviewed by a company's AI recruiter. Victor misstated his qualifications and said he would work for about $60,000 a year when he wanted $140,000 to $150,000, the recruiter would not go above $90,000, and the two bots then booked a follow-up without him before getting stuck thanking each other. The Register's writer argues this is a warning for AI agents that are meant to negotiate or shop for people.
notes: Read in full. The video was not viewed; all details come from The Register's description.
